name: Weezy Blue
lede: Weezy Blue is a vivid greenish blue whose own origin is undocumented in our sources, though its ISCC-NBS paint-chip block holds several older, better-documented names for almost the same color.

sections.title: Origin undocumented
sections.body:
Our sources trace Weezy Blue only to the web; who coined it and when is undocumented here [1]. It falls in the ISCC-NBS 1955 system's block for vivid greenish blue, about three units from that block's center [1]. That block holds a cluster of older names for nearly the same chip: Bright Greenish Blue, Coeru and Leum, plus Caeruleum, which Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates to 1859, and Italian Blue, which they date to 1912, plate 33 [1]. None of those names is documented as Weezy Blue's own source, but they show the chip itself has a much longer paper trail than this one name does [1].

Its closest measured look-alike is [[united-nations-blue|United Nations Blue]], read as almost the same color; [[carolina-blue|Carolina Blue]] sits further out, read as bluer [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds this color in only 3 of them, about 0.01 percent, as photographed, rarer than 88 percent of our named colors [2]. A color chip with this much naming history behind it can still be scarce on real canvases: a paint-chip block is a system of classification, not a record of what painters actually used [2].
